identity.name: Magnesium diglutamate
identity.chemical_class: Magnesium salt of L-glutamic acid (glutamate flavour-enhancer salt)

function.mechanism: Supplies free glutamate ions that enhance umami perception and can support sodium reduction by maintaining savoury intensity.

adi.basis: Group ADI for glutamic acid and glutamates (E620-E625), expressed as glutamic acid (EFSA 2017 re-evaluation).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA set a group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day and identified scenarios where exposure could exceed the ADI; subsequent EU legislation tightened uses/levels for glutamates.

fda.cfr_citation: No direct magnesium diglutamate listing found in current Title 21 eCFR search; related glutamate GRAS entries include 21 CFR 182.1, 21 CFR 182.1500, and 21 CFR 182.1516.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group context for L-glutamic acid and its ammonium, calcium, magnesium, monosodium, and potassium salts).

concerns.summary: A human-lymphocyte in vitro study (2020) reported concentration-dependent increases in chromosome damage and related endpoints for magnesium diglutamate, with stronger effects at higher concentrations.
A 2024 molecular docking paper suggested plausible interactions of magnesium diglutamate with DNA damage-response targets; this is mechanistic and not direct in vivo toxicity evidence.
An Allium cepa assay reported chromosomal-abnormality signals for magnesium diglutamate, but the non-mammalian model has limited direct relevance for human dietary risk quantification.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA lists ADI as not specified for the L-glutamate salt group, including magnesium salt.
EFSA retained authorization context for glutamates but set a finite group ADI and called for exposure control.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2017 group exposure assessment for glutamates (E620-E625) identified ADI exceedance scenarios in parts of the population.

risk_assessment.rationale: E625 is not banned and remains in an authorized glutamate group, but EFSA established a finite group ADI and found exceedance risk in some populations, while direct additive-specific human safety data are limited and in vitro genotoxicity findings exist at higher test concentrations.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day for E620-E625
EU follow-up restrictions after EFSA exposure conclusions
JECFA ADI not specified historical group position
No direct Title 21 CFR listing for magnesium diglutamate found in current eCFR search
Recent E625-specific evidence is mainly in vitro/mechanistic, not robust human longitudinal data
No IARC Group 1/2A/2B classification identified for E625
